summary: Kershaw County, SC Forestry Commission tower; one of two built in the 1946-47 fiscal year; listed as removed and demolished, with no date.

facts.status_note: Forest Lookouts lists it as Removed, with no date; OpenStreetMap names it Demolished

events.note: A Forest Lookouts page quotes the commission's annual report for 7/1/1946 to 6/30/1947 as calling it one of two lookout towers constructed that year; the report itself was not read, and the exact month is not given
System-wide: the commission closed its fire tower system on October 1, 1993; the removal date of this tower is not given

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The commission's own history gives October 1, 1993 for closing its fire tower system; the Post and Courier says the system was decommissioned in 1994. The story reports both dates.

sources.title: Facebook post on the closing of the commission's fire lookout towers

notes_for_editor: The 1946-47 build date is the commission's fiscal year as quoted on the Forest Lookouts page; the annual report itself was not read. No design, height, staffing, fire or access source was found, so none is stated. Two sources agree the tower is gone, but neither dates its removal. The first-tower history conflicts on detail: the Post and Courier says the 1930 Camden tower was built by the Civilian Conservation Corps, while the commission says it was assembled by the Kershaw County Forestry Association. That is not used here.
